page: Amazon Web Services r8in.96xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by Intel x86_64 processors delivering 384 dedicated vCPUs across 192 physical cores at speeds up to 3.9 GHz. Utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture with two threads per physical core, the instance provides 3072.0 GB of total system memory, establishing a resource ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Network infrastructure on the instance supports a baseline network bandwidth of 600 Gbps, enabling high-throughput data transfers for scale-out architectures and data ingestion pipelines. The configuration contains zero bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPU accelerators, meaning persistent disk storage relies entirely on network-attached storage services over the network interface.

By consolidating massive compute and memory resources into a single server, r8in.96xlarge provides high resource density for workloads that would otherwise require multi-instance clustering. The absence of local disk drives requires high-throughput storage attachments, an architectural trade-off offset by the 600 Gbps networking fabric. The instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching grids, big data analytics engines, and enterprise enterprise-resource-planning (ERP) systems.
